title: Private/VPC: Ephemeral-node network reconciliation and air-gap certification PRD
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Summary: This PRD defines requirements and acceptance criteria for ensuring that ephemeral worker/control-plane nodes in Private/VPC deployments can safely join, reconcile network policies, rotate certificates, and be upgraded in both online and air-gapped environments. The goal is to provide deterministic network and artifact verification (mirror + signature) and a clear operator handoff for staged rollouts and rollbacks.

Background/Problem: Customers running Redwood Private often operate ephemeral scaling nodes (burst pools, spot-like worker fleets, temporary inference nodes) and strict egress/air-gap constraints. During upgrades or scale events we see two classes of failures: (1) transient network policy mismatches that isolate nodes from control-plane or mirrors, and (2) artifact provenance failures when mirror syncs are delayed or unsigned. Both can cause stuck upgrades, silent drift, or operator uncertainty.

Goals:
- Define preflight network checks and deterministic reconciliation for ephemeral nodes that run in isolated VPC segments.
- Specify artifact mirror + signature verification for air-gapped bootstraps and operator-visible validation artifacts.
- Prescribe upgrade sequencing (control-plane -> registry sync -> data-plane) and an operator handoff checklist with rollback triggers.

Scope:
- In scope: network preflight tooling, agent-level MTLS handoff steps, mirror index signing verification, canary cohort rules for ephemeral pools, runbook text.
- Out of scope: redesign of on-prem registry product, cloud provider-level firewall automation, new KMS integrations beyond existing KMS patterns.

Stakeholders: Product, Security, Runtime Engineering, Private Deploy Ops, Solutions Eng.

Success metrics:
- <5% upgrade failures caused by ephemeral-node network mismatch in canary cohorts.
- Zero accepted upgrades in air-gap environments without a verified signed index.
- Operator time-to-diagnose reduced by 60% via preflight checks and runbook automation.
acceptance_criteria: Network preflight: A preflight utility returns PASS/CHECKLIST that confirms: control-plane reachable on required ports, mirror endpoint reachable (or offline mirror detected), MTLS handshake possible with existing cluster certs, and required CIDR egress rules are present. Tests: manual and automated preflight must pass in >= 95% of test runs in lab VPCs.

Signed mirror verification: Air-gap bootstrap process refuses to accept a mirrored image set unless a signed index file (signed by customer-approved key) is present and its SHA256 manifests match checksums in the agent. Failure paths are logged and surfaced to operator console with exact mismatch details.

Certificate continuity: During a staged control-plane upgrade, ephemeral nodes must complete an MTLS handoff where old certs continue to validate for in-flight sessions for a configurable grace window (default 5 minutes). Tests include simulated cert rotation with active inference traffic and zero dropped RPCs for in-flight requests beyond transient retries.

Upgrade sequencing: The platform must support a preflight -> canary-control-plane -> mirror-sync -> canary-workers -> wide-rollout sequence with automated gating. If telemetry (heartbeat/trace) falls below a threshold, automated rollback of the latest life-cycle step triggers and is reversible by operator. Playbook and automation documented.

Operator runbook & UI: The Console must surface a 'Private Upgrade Safety' page that includes preflight results, mirror signature verification, cohort membership for ephemeral pools, and one-click abort/rollback. Acceptance requires mock demo and UX review sign-off from Design and Solutions Eng.

Chaos/partition test: In a simulated partition (partial egress blocked to mirror), the system must either fail the upgrade safely (no partial rollout beyond canary) or continue only when manual approval provided. Telemetry and audit events recorded for every decision point.

Audit & telemetry: All preflight runs, signature validations, cert rotations, and rollback decisions must generate audit entries with at least: timestamp, node id, artifact index hash, operator id, and decision outcome. These events must be queryable in Console within 10s of the event in hosted telemetry (or exported as a log bundle for air-gapped installs).
notes: Implementation patterns recommended: reuse existing agent bootstrap path and extend with a preflight plugin that performs MTLS and CIDR checks. Add a signed-index validator module (verifies a signature over a manifest list).
Test artifacts: create a reproducible lab topology with 3 control-plane nodes, 2 ephemeral worker cohorts, a mirrored on-prem registry, and an egress-proxy that can simulate partitioning.

References: Confluence PRD draft (https://confluence.company/PRD/private-ephemeral-recon), Design mockups in Drive (https://drive.company/ux/private-upgrade-safe-page), related Linear tickets ENG-29401, PM-582019.

Tradeoffs: Requiring signed index files in all air-gap bootstraps raises operator friction for small customers; mitigation is an escape hatch documented in runbook requiring two-operator approvals and audit logging.
